statement: Let d ≥ 3, b = d − 1, and 0 < θ ≤ b−1/2. Let π be a probability law on X2 with both marginals equal to ν, invariant under the simultaneous action of Aut(Td). Suppose that g = (ge) assigns a measurable real function of X to every directed edge, with Eνg2 e < ∞, and that for each fixed γ ∈ Aut(Td) and directed edge e, gγe(γx) = ge(x) for ν-almost every x. Here γ(i, j) = (γi, γj). For the two coordinate arrays X, X′ under π, set De = ge(X) − ge(X′ ), S = EπD2 e. 28 The value of S is independent of the directed edge. There is a constant Cd < ∞, depending only on d, such that for every integer r ≥ 1 and every simple path v0, . . . , vr, Eπ   r X i=1 D(vi−1,vi) !2   ≤ CdrS, Eπ   r X i=1 D(vi,vi−1) !2   ≤ CdrS. (6.1) In particular, take π to be the (X, X′)-marginal of the joining in Proposition 5.1. Then this holds for the differences De(t) in (5.7) at each fixed finite time, with S = S(t).
